Priya Desai: Quick sync: three enterprise customers asked for a clear, low-friction upgrade path from an air-gapped minimal installer to our full on-prem distro. want to agree on what the conversion/rollback contract looks like.
Mira Patel: Key constraints: non-destructive conversion, no forced reboots, and preserved config+secrets. conversion must be idempotent and provide a dry-run mode.
Samir Khan: Implementation idea: ship a converter binary that runs in two phases: (1) artifact verification + SBOM validation, (2) staged component enablement with health checks. converter writes a migration plan to /var/lib/redwood/migration.json.
Nia Rivera: Security: converter must validate signatures against customer-provisioned root keys, support offline KMS wrapping/unwrapping, and rotate ephemeral admin tokens after conversion. include audit events.
Owen Blake: Support asks: include concise preflight checks (disk, ports, kernel modules), an opt-in debug bundle uploader (customer endpoint), and explicit rollback steps that revert only enabled components.
Priya Desai: Launch criteria suggestion: 1) converter dry-run produces deterministic plan; 2) full conversion tested v1.0-lite -> v1.0-full and v1.0-full -> v1.1-full; 3) post-conversion healthcheck passes (model runtime + control plane).
Mira Patel: Prioritize customers with tight upgrade SLAs. propose pilot with one fintech and one healthcare customer. limit GA to customers who pass pilot checklist.
Samir Khan: Est effort: prototyping converter spike (1 sprint), implement verifier + migration planner (2 sprints), end-to-end upgrade tests + docs (1 sprint).
Nia Rivera: I'll draft the security checklist and example key provisioning flow. will include sample commands for HSM-backed setups.
deploy-bot: Epic created PRIV-CONVERT-211 and linked this thread.
Priya Desai: Action items: Samir -> converter design doc (4d), Nia -> security checklist + HSM patterns (6d), Owen -> preflight checklist + support playbook (5d). follow-up 30m next Wed.
